newsitem.title: ALBANIA: U.S. airlifts 331 more evacuees from Albania.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlifts 331 more evacuees from Albania.

text.p: U.S. military helicopters airlifted 331 Americans and other foreigners from Albania's capital Tirana on Saturday before darkness forced a halt to the day's operations, a Marine officer said.

The operation, suspended on Friday after two Marine Cobra helicopters were fired on, restarted at dawn with a steady trickle of evacuees boarding Chinook, Sea Stallion and Huey helicopters at the U.S. diplomatic compound.

"We are taking them out just as fast as we can. This operation will carry on until the ambassador tells us to wrap it up," Marine Colonel Emerson Gardner, commander of the rescue force, told reporters in the compound.
Saturday's evacuees, taken to Brindisi in southeast Italy, took the total number of Americans and 31 other nationalities flown out by the Marines to more than 700.
"We don't continue the operations at night because there's too much gunfire," one Marine officer said.
Those evacuated on Saturday included Bulgarian embassy staff, more than 20 Russians including eight embassy staff, Jordanians, Greeks, Dutch and several Albanians with U.S. visas.
The American operation began on Thursday after Albania's anarchy spread to Tirana, with gunfire in the streets and widespread looting of armouries and food stores.
On Friday, two U.S. helicopters were fired on, while an Italian helicopter was also hit. German troops mounting a helicopter rescue exchanged fire with gunmen on the ground, wounding one Albanian.
Military rescues by Italian, American, German and French forces have brought close to 2,000 people out of Albania.

Tirana was quieter on Saturday, with the level of gunfire greatly reduced. Authorities facing a nationwide slide into anarchy have sought to restore order by parading armoured vehicles on the streets and raising police pay.
